title: Torso Limbs
author: Mateus
desc:
Superset based bodybuilding program.

Go to failure or 0 RIR on everything that won't decapitate or crush you if you do so. 

Stick to a good standard of form without obsessing over it (at least a 2 second eccentric, 1 second pause at the stretched position, as big of a stretch as possible, explosive concentric, no hip involvement).

Didn't include any rear delt work as, in my experience, they grow just fine without isolation, but you can add them as a superset to your ab work. I really enjoy skiers, meadows rear delt swings or the single arm cross body cable stuff.

In movements where it's safe, do lengthened supersets after failure, especially if they have shit resistance profiles (back work, incline curls, etc.) or just straight up do lengthened partials instead of full rom.

😢🤳 You before program
💪🏿🤵🏿‍♂️ You after program

ss.note: Stick to 60-90 seconds of rest after doing the 2 exercises in all the supersets.
Do lengthened supersets past failure or lengthened partials from the beginning. After you can't move the weight, stand up and do shrugs to failure for some free upper trap volume.
Drag an incline bench to a cable stack and grab a pair of dumbbells. Good supersets without equipment hogging too much.
Do lengthened partials. Stop right before you hit a 90 degree angle between the upper and lower arm. This will allow you to use a shit ton of weight and get a psychotic stretch.
If you can't superset these 2 movements, just one then the other with 2 minutes of test between sets.
Go past failure. Lengthened partials are an option.
Lengthened superset after failure.
Do lengthened partials. Pause at the stretched position.
Go super slow with a big pause in the stretched position. More adductor flexibility is always better.
Don't kip or flop around. Explosive concentric, slow eccentric, pause at the stretched position.
Do some horizontal shrugs (aka Kelso Shrugs) after failure.
Supposed to be a Seated EZ Bar BTN Press, but I don't have a premium version of the app and can't create more exercises. Use the leg holder thingy as back support.
